title: Whether a provider url passed for one call may choose a private address, in three languages
pins: Whether a provider url passed for ONE call (`using(provider, model, {url})`) is refused before any request when it names a loopback, private, link-local, shared, unique-local, unspecified or cloud metadata address, written as a literal in the spellings an OS resolver reads (IPv6 forms that carry an IPv4 address included), or named by a stock hosts file, and whether a host is judged exactly as written: an escape, any character a hostname or address literal may not hold, or a format, invisible or IDNA deviation character, is refused rather than decoded or converted, and whether a non-ASCII host is refused with its own code (non_ascii_host_use_punycode) while its punycode form is sent. A per-call url is chosen by whoever builds the call, so a url that reaches 169.254.169.254 or a service behind the firewall in one language and is refused in another is an SSRF hole in whichever accepts it, and nothing errors to say so. Configured urls are the operator's and are deliberately not checked; they appear only as controls, together with the one explicit configuration opt-out and the proof that the call itself cannot turn it on.
scope: The openai provider and one named openai-compatible entry, entered through Prism.text().using() in each language. Address literals in decimal, octal, hex, shortened, IPv6, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, SIIT IPv4-translated and ISATAP spellings, the RHEL, openSUSE, Debian and macOS hosts-file names and names under localhost.localdomain, userinfo in front of the host, local and metadata names with case and trailing-dot variation, percent escapes in names, address literals and IPv6 literals, characters no host may hold, a backslash in the authority, zero-width joiners, other invisible characters and the IDNA deviation characters (U+1E9E included), non-ASCII hosts (an international name, names that fail the IDNA2008 bidi and hyphen rules, full-width digits) and the punycode forms of international names, IPv6 literals with a dotted IPv4 tail (public, and carrying a private address under ISATAP or NAT64), an empty written host, a public name with a trailing dot, one non-http scheme, and the configuration controls. NOT covered: a public hostname that RESOLVES to a private address (no language resolves names here, by design: the check makes no network call), DNS rebinding, the reference's other providers and custom providers (each language's own regression tests cover those), and the refusal message, which is outside the contract.
construction: Native PHP manager entered through Prism::text()->using() with Laravel's HTTP fake and stray requests prevented, reading the package's own config/prism.php against each row's environment; native TypeScript Prism.text().using() with fetch captured; native Python Prism.text().using() with the default transport's send captured and DNS and sockets refused. Every fixture answers 500, because only whether a request went out matters. Each observation is `dispatched` and the refusal code, and nothing else: tools/per-call-url-guard/contract.mjs refuses any other field and any row both dispatched and refused.
findings: 89 of 89 rows agree on the fix branches (prism, prism-ts and prism-py `fix/g366-per-call-host-followups`). Against the code before that fix, the 12 rows added with it and the changed pcu-0055 fail 8 rows in PHP and 6 in each port: all three accepted U+1E9E inside localhost and in a public name and accepted the unicode international name; PHP refused the bidi-rule and hyphen-rule names with private_address_refused where the ports SENT them, and refused public IPv6 literals with a dotted IPv4 tail where the ports sent them. A non-ASCII per-call host is now refused with non_ascii_host_use_punycode in every language, before any conversion, and its punycode form is sent; no language runs IDNA on a per-call host any more. Before that, on the code before the G-365 fix, 77 of 77 rows ALSO agreed while 14 of the 22 rows added with it were SENT in all three languages, and on the code before the as-written host rule 43 of the first 55 agreed. The zero-width joiner rows, and the Persian name that needs one, record no refusal code in any language, because each language's clean-url check refuses them before the guard runs; the guard on its own refuses them too, which each language's unit rows assert, since this suite only enters through using(). Agreement here is a conclusion about behaviour, not about safety: the three guards follow one spec, so a shared misreading of it would agree here too. A hostname that resolves to a private address is not refused, in any language, because no language resolves names here.

discrimination.gap: No mutation probe is delivered for this suite. Four coarse negative controls: the code before the per-call guard fails 29 to 30 of the first 34 rows in every language; the code before the as-written host rule fails 12 of the first 55; the code before the G-365 fix sends 14 of the 22 rows added with it, in all three languages, while every row still agrees; and the code before the G-366 fix fails 8 rows in PHP and 6 in each port.

php.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with php --check. PRISM_PHP_SRC points it at a prism checkout (CI uses the default branch); without it, it reads the installed reference in runners/php.

ts.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with ts --check; it reads the built sibling prism-ts/dist, or PRISM_TS_DIST.

py.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with py --check; it imports the installed package, or PRISM_PY_SRC.
